subject: Discovery recap: Finly p95 latency & streaming concurrency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tim O'Leary <tim@finly.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, infra@finly.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Finly p95 latency & streaming concurrency

Thanks for the call earlier, Tim — really helpful context. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the success criteria you outlined, and proposed next steps. Please flag anything I missed or got wrong.

Summary of pain points
- End users see noticeable stalls in the streaming chat UX when multiple people are active (~1500 concurrent sessions).
- Current infra struggles with p95 tail latency on token streaming and with cold-starts impacting UX.
- Prefix caching and reuse across similar prompts is inconsistent, so effective throughput drops under load.

Current stack (from call)
- Self-hosted inference on GCP using Triton + custom batching layer.
- Mix of smaller open models for quick responses and larger models for longer-form tasks.
- Frontend uses client-side streaming; backend aggregates partial chunks and forwards as they arrive.

Quantified success criteria you mentioned
- p95 per-token/response latency target: <= 300ms for streaming responses in typical sessions.
- Sustained concurrency target: ~1,500 concurrent active chat sessions during peak.
- Throughput: ~4 responses per session on average, ~120 tokens per response.
- Streaming UX: sub-200ms first-byte for short replies, smooth incremental updates (no long stalls).

Risks & constraints
- Memory footprint on existing GPU types (V100/P100) is tight; can't easily swap to huge instances without cost pushback.
- Regulatory constraint: log retention policy requires audit logs to be retained for 18 months (mentioned by infra@finly.com).

Attachments referenced
- finly-infra-diagram.png (infra diagram you shared during the call)

Proposed next steps
1) Tech deep-dive with Aditya (solutions engineer) to review token-level traces, batching behavior, and KV cache opportunities — suggested: Thu, Nov 5 at 10am PT.
2) We’ll run a short perf checklist: reproduce a 1500-concurrency synthetic test, capture p95 numbers for streaming vs non-streaming, and evaluate caching impact.
3) If numbers look good, share a baseline Redwood config (batching, kv cache, quantization profile) and an estimate for Dedicated capacity sizing.

If that all sounds right, I’ll lock the tech session and invite Aditya. Thanks again for your time — excited to see if we can get you to the p95 targets without a full infra rewrite.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly p95 latency & streaming concurrency

Thanks Marissa — solid summary and aligned on the targets. Couple of clarifications / extra details: 

- Concurrency: 1,500 active sessions is our expected peak; sustained for ~30–45 minutes during business hours. Spikes to ~2,200 for short bursts.
- Token profile: ~120 tokens/response average but distribution is long-tailed — ~10% of responses go >400 tokens.
- Cold-starts: our biggest UX issue is the 8–12s stall when larger-model workers spin up; those stalls are what users notice as broken streaming.
- Cost sensitivity: we can consider bigger instances but finance will push back unless we can show clear unit-cost improvements vs current ops.

I've attached the infra diagram we referenced. Also, infra@finly.com asked to capture what logs/metrics we can share prior to the deep dive (traces, perf dumps, current batching params).

Tim
Head of Product
Finly
tim@finly.com

Great — thanks for the clarifications, Tim. I scheduled the tech deep-dive with Aditya for Thu, Nov 5 at 10:00am PT and sent a calendar invite to the same addresses. Agenda for the deep-dive: 

- 15m: walk through current infra diagram & token distribution (Finly)
- 30m: Aditya to review batching config, KV cache opportunities, and streaming path (traces)
- 10m: sizing/quantization options and quick cost sensitivity check
- 5m: agree next deliverables and timeline (PoC perf test; baseline config)

Prep requested from Finly before the call:
- perf traces / token-level p95 numbers if available (or synthetic test script)
- current batching params and worker types
- any constraints on introducing an intermediary cache or short-lived warm workers

I'll share a short pre-read (1–2 pages) with what data points we need and a template for the synthetic test. Aditya — looping you in to confirm the agenda and whether you want any extra log formats ahead of the call.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
Marissa
